slides.title: RMS estate review: cost, condition and first data products

scqa: The estate holds 174.3 TiB across databases, the object store and file shares. The object store is 74.8% of that and the file shares 25.0%. The 20 databases, with 1006 tables, are only 0.2% of the bytes.

Priced savings reach 1,174.4 USD a month at reference list prices, and three strategies address 100.0% of the bytes that all strategies reach. Database rows are in poor condition: 81.7% have empty required-looking fields and 71.8% of sampled rows carry personal-data markers.
What should the owner do first to cut cost and prepare the first data products?

Start with the archive move for buckets not written for over a year, worth 986.5 USD a month, after checking read frequency. Then confirm duplicate objects and prepare reference and channel data as de-identified or aggregated products.

points: The whole estate holds 174.3 TiB: the object store holds 130.3 TiB and the file shares hold 43.6 TiB.
By share of the estate, the object store is 74.8%, the file shares 25.0% and the databases 0.2%.
The object store has 23.0m objects in 106 buckets, and its largest bucket alone holds 86.3 TiB, which is 66.2% of the store.
The file shares hold 1.5m files in 16 shares; how much of that is duplicated has not yet been measured.
The databases hold 351.3 GiB in 1006 tables, and the largest databases account for 99.7% of those bytes.

slides.title: A handful of databases hold almost all database bytes

points: Exact duplicate rows are 1.5% of rows, a low figure; the duplication problem lies in copied tables and objects, not repeated rows.
Degraded rows are 23.0% of rows, and 81.7% carry empty required-looking fields, which limits what can be sold without cleansing.
Personal-data markers appear in 71.8% of the 1.0m rows sampled, so de-identification or aggregation is a standing preparation step for products.
Bytes not written for over a year are 15.4% of database bytes, and 368 tables are empty.
These ratios are estimates from complete passes where tables allowed and stratified samples elsewhere.
slides.title: Rows are rarely duplicated but often incomplete, degraded or personal
Which data products to stand up first

points: 8 product candidates were scored for readiness; the three leading ones are all grade C and none is ready for release as it stands.

Reference and master-data licensing: Reference and master-data licensing: grade C, 87 tables, 123,394,159 rows (est.); to prepare: 62.0% of supporting tables carry PII markers: de-identify or aggregate before any release

Content catalogue and recommendation corpus: Content catalogue, recommendation and licensing corpus: grade C, 98 tables, 157,855,990 rows (est.); to prepare: 74.0% of supporting tables carry PII markers: de-identify or aggregate before any release

Channel and telco engagement analytics: Channel / telco engagement analytics (USSD, SMS, app): grade C, 57 tables, 116,781,903 rows (est.); to prepare: 79.0% of supporting tables carry PII markers: de-identify or aggregate before any release
Rights are settled by the owner's declaration, so preparation is technical: de-identify or aggregate, then cleanse. The remaining candidates need cleansing before they are worth building.
slides.title: Three grade C candidates lead, and each needs de-identification or aggregation first
What is still unmeasured

points: Measures cover 638 of 1006 tables, which is 63.4%; the remaining ratios are estimated from stratified samples.
40 of 106 object-store buckets could not be read, so every object-store figure covers only the readable buckets.
The file shares hold 43.6 TiB in 1.5m files, but only sizes and dates were recorded, so duplication cannot be stated.
One database connection, artists_app, could not be read because read access is pending, so it sits outside every database figure.
slides.title: Measurement gaps are specific, and each has a defined way to close it

points: Check read frequency on the 43 cold buckets, then archive 41.9 TiB: 986.5 USD a month.
Hash-check 7.7 TiB of duplicate candidates before deleting: 180.3 USD a month.
Reconcile the 40 unreadable buckets with the provider; the figures above exclude them.
Prepare de-identified reference and channel copies; tidy cold tables, 5.9 USD a month, alongside.
